observations: OpenDHT defines HASH_LEN as 20 bytes and InfoHash as Hash<HASH_LEN>, so its lookup-key type is exactly 160 bits.

OpenDHT Hash(const uint8_t* h, size_t data_len) constructs from fromBytes; fromBytes copies the first N input bytes directly when at least N bytes are supplied. This constructor does not call crypto::hash. The separate static Hash::get(...) method is the API that hashes arbitrary input.
OpenDHT DHT get APIs accept const InfoHash& key, so a caller can pass an InfoHash constructed from the exact 20 raw Git SHA-1 bytes rather than invoking Hash::get and rehashing them.

Git object verification is locally reproducible from canonical object bytes: Git formats the object header as <type> <obj-len> plus a terminating NUL and hashes that header followed by object data; Git also compares the recomputed object id with the expected object id when validating loose objects.

Therefore the exact Git SHA-1 bytes can serve as an OpenDHT lookup key at the API/key-representation layer, and any returned candidate commit content can be accepted only after reconstructing Git canonical framing and recomputing the expected object id.

OpenDHT key compatibility does not imply data availability. This slice established no independently pre-existing OpenDHT value at the target key and performed no DHT network lookup, put, publication, republishing, pinning, hosted query, or external mutation.
probe.inference: Unlike BEP 44 immutable-item addressing, OpenDHT's raw InfoHash constructor permits an exact 160-bit caller-chosen lookup key without mandatory rehashing. This supplies a protocol/API-level exact-key identity bridge to a SHA-1 Git object id, while local canonical Git hashing can reject substituted bytes. The remaining necessary condition is independently pre-existing residency of the desired canonical Git payload under that exact key; no evidence for that condition was established here.
